title: Align-for-Fusion: Harmonizing Triple Preferences via Dual-oriented Diffusion for Cross-domain Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Personalized sequential recommendation must predict appropriate items from users' behavioral sequences, while data sparsity and interest drift motivate using behaviors from other domains.

gap.claim: Existing cross-domain sequential recommendation methods align representations across domains and mechanically combine them, overlooking fine-grained multi-domain fusion.

contributions.claim: The authors propose HorizonRec, an align-for-fusion framework using dual-oriented diffusion models to harmonize triple preferences for cross-domain sequential recommendation.

The framework introduces Mixed-conditioned Distribution Retrieval, using distributions retrieved from users' authentic behavioral logic as a bridge across three domains for consistent multi-domain preference modeling.
The framework introduces Dual-oriented Preference Diffusion to extract preferences aligned with users' authentic interests from each domain under supervision from the mixed representation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments and analyses on four cross-domain sequential recommendation datasets from two distinct platforms to assess HorizonRec's effectiveness and robustness.
The authors report that the experiments analyze the mechanism of fine-grained fusion across triple domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation predicts items from user behavior sequences.
Cross-domain behavior is used to address data sparsity and interest drift, but existing methods mechanically align and fuse domains.
HorizonRec uses distribution retrieval and dual-oriented preference diffusion to model and fuse triple-domain preferences.
The authors report experiments and analyses across four datasets from two platforms.
The authors report that code and datasets are available online.

source_observation.claim: Existing methods mechanically combine representations after cross-domain alignment and overlook fine-grained fusion.

interpretation.claim: Cross-domain systems may need fusion mechanisms that preserve domain-specific, target-relevant preference signals instead of relying only on representation alignment.

application.claim: For multi-domain recommendation, evaluate whether fusion explicitly suppresses irrelevant cross-domain noise and emphasizes interests relevant to the target domain.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that fine-grained fusion is superior for domains, datasets, or settings beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: No quantitative results, baselines, or statistical details are provided.
The four datasets, two platforms, and evaluation protocols are not identified.
The abstract does not specify the diffusion architecture, training procedure, or computational cost.
The abstract does not provide details needed to assess reproducibility beyond the reported code and dataset availability.
